Three pieces, one from each of Lists A (faster, technical agility), B (lyrical, expressive) and C (varied traditions/styles); at least one must be accompanied. sections: Scales & technical work
Scales: G, D majors from open strings, 1 oct., separate bows, even notes or long tonic (candidate's choice); A minor from bottom A to a 5th, separate bows, even notes. (All three played.)
Sight-reading

4 bars (4/4) or 6 bars (2/4); time: 4/4 or 2/4; new features: 1st position; crotchet and quaver note values, crotchet rests; notes separately bowed; mf; new keys: G, D majors; range: g–c′, d′–g′. Unaccompanied; 30 seconds to prepare; parameters are cumulative from earlier grades.
Aural & other tests
Clap the pulse; clap back rhythm echoes of two 2-bar phrases; sing back two 1-bar echoes (tonic–mediant, major); answer a question on dynamics or articulation of a piece.

comps: Face-to-face (all instruments): 3 pieces x 22 = 66 (each piece: fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8); technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (2 x 10). Total 100. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No section has to be passed individually. Per-piece bands: 19-22 Distinction, 16-18 Merit, 13-15 Pass.

Face-to-face bowed strings: Initial 11 min; G1-3 13 min; G4-5 18 min; G6-7 23 min; G8 28 min. Harp: Initial 13 min; G1-3 15 min; G4-5 20 min; G6-7 25 min; G8 30 min. Section order is the candidate's choice (default: bowed strings pieces first; harp technical work first). Digital: no exam length stated.

Pieces come from the separate repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/strings). Initial-Grade 3: any 3 pieces (4 on digital Repertoire-only), max one duet (bowed strings only; upper part, partner live or pre-recorded on a bowed string instrument, never piano), max one unaccompanied piece. Grades 4-5: any 3, max one unaccompanied. Grades 6-8: list split into Group A and Group B; choose 3 with at least one from each group; max one unaccompanied. Own composition may replace one listed piece at every grade (duration Initial 30-40s rising to 3-4 min at G7-8; any notation to G5, staff notation required G6-8; copy given to examiner/uploaded). Violin: a piece/set from the Scottish traditional fiddle list at the same grade may replace one piece (max one unaccompanied or fiddle item); G6-8 one piece may be played on viola from the Viola list (technical work and supporting tests on violin). Viola: G6-8 one piece may be on violin from the Violin list. Double bass: max one all-pizzicato piece. Harp: Initial-G3 pieces playable on pedal or lever harp unless marked. Pieces published with accompaniment must be accompanied (single instrument, piano unless approved). Face-to-face: recorded accompaniment/backing track allowed up to Grade 3, live accompaniment from Grade 4; page turner allowed G6-8. Vibrato expected from Grade 5 (bowed). Repeats of 4 bars or fewer observed, longer repeats omitted unless stated; D.C./D.S. observed; cadenzas only if stated; memory optional (no extra marks). Teachers may help tune up to G5; G6-8 candidates tune unaided.

Two pathways, same entry process; exam filmed as one continuous take. Technical work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance criteria 20 = 100. Technical work played as one unit in listed order (before, after or between pieces); bowed strings play the bowing exercise (not at Initial) then EITHER one fixed set of scales/arpeggios/technical exercises (set A or set B - every item in the set is played, with bowings specified, from memory) OR two studies (G1-5) / two orchestral extracts from different groups (G6-8), candidate's choice; harp plays the listed scales/arpeggios/exercises OR two studies OR (pedal harp G6-8) two orchestral extracts. Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100, no technical work or supporting tests. Same grade boundaries as face-to-face. Backing tracks/recorded accompaniment allowed at all grades in digital exams.
sections: Technical work

1) Bowing: candidate picks a G8 scale/arpeggio, examiner picks a G5-7 bowing. EITHER 2) tonal centres C, C#/Db, D, Eb, F 3 oct (scales separate or three octaves to a bow; arpeggios separate or slurred nine); chromatic from Eb, F, G 2 oct (separate or slurred twelve); diminished 7ths from D#, F, G (separate or slurred eight). Min: scales and arpeggios dotted crotchet 88, 7ths crotchet 92. Technical exercises (crotchet = 88): Eb major thirds 2 oct, C major sixths 2 oct, G major octaves 1 oct. OR 3) Orchestral extracts (music allowed): prepare three (Orchester Probespiel: Viola), play two: tone - Brahms Haydn Variations (Var. 4) or Strauss Don Juan; bowing - Prokofiev Classical Symphony IV or Tchaikovsky Sym. 6 I; left hand - Bartók Divertimento III or Brahms Sym. 3 I.
Supporting tests

Sight reading (compulsory) + aural OR improvisation. Sight reading (30s prep, about two grades below the exam; cumulative): adds 2/2 and changing time signatures; duplets; double stops with two stopped notes (not in sequences); keys all major and minor keys. Aural: 12-16-bar harmonised major or minor piece in 2, 3, 4, 6 or 5 time - time signature, dynamics, articulation (one hearing); three other characteristics; with a copy, locate three changes as pitch or rhythm. Improvisation: stylistic - 16 bars over piano (impressionistic or irregular dance, 5 time, adds C#/F minor, all chords incl. 7ths, 9ths, suspensions); motivic - 12-16-bar unaccompanied response to a 1-bar motif; harmonic - unaccompanied over a chord sequence (8 bars x2; all chords, 7ths, 9ths, suspensions; keys C, D, E, F, G, A, Bb major; A, B, C#, D, E, F#, G minor).

exams.name: ATCL
exams.full: Associate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 4/5); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0949/4
comps: None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ATCL repertoire list for viola, read from the Trinity PDF (30 entries). Programmes must consist of a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified. Programmes may use list pieces, a mix of list and own-choice pieces, or only own-choice pieces; any programme with own-choice repertoire must be pre-approved and own-choice pieces must be of comparable demand. Performance durations: ATCL 32-38 min, LTCL 37-43 min, FTCL 42-48 min. Refer to the syllabus for guidance on inclusion of unaccompanied items. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction of the programme (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required at ATCL.

General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required. Learning outcomes add contextual understanding and the candidate's own musical voice.
